title: First clarinet lessons: the high school bandmaster and Buster Bailey
summary: Started clarinet in the high school band under Professor Tulesty; his distant cousin Buster Bailey, working with Erskine Tate, gave him lessons.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: But wait a minute. We -- just -- we better not jump too much. When you -- when did you first begin to play clarinet?
In the high school band.
Oh, at the high school.
Yes, that's right.
Who taught you there?
Old man Tulesty started me off. He was the professor -- the conductor. But I finished up --
Well, how do you spell that?
Well, that's a German name, Tulesty, I think T-u-l-e-s-t-y, Tulesty.
Oh, I see.
Because that's the head man of the school, he was named German, descending the wife, the son, and then Buster -- I went with Buster.
Now, Buster in the book it says (unintelligible), he was a cousin of yours.
Right, distant cousin of mine, and I went with him because he was working with Erskine Tate at the Vendome Theater, and I used to go down there, and he would come over and take lessons.
Well, was Buster about the same age as you?
I think I'm a little older than Buster.
I see. But he had tuition on clarinet.
Oh, yes.
That was in Memphis.
Indeed -- that's right. But when he was a kid, he used to [play regular] out there before I did.
I think we started talking about Buster. We ought to mention the fact we're talking about Buster Bailey.
Right.
Yes, so he really helped you --
He did.
-- in addition to the school.
